content:
to	the	elves	and	climbed	carefully	back	towards	the	Gate.
Great	weariness	began	to	come	over	him;	but	it	was	well
before	midnight	when	he	clambered	up	the	rope	again—it
was	still	where	he	had	left	it.	He	untied	it	and	hid	it,	and
then	 he	 sat	 down	 on	 the	 wall	 and	 wondered	 anxiously
what	would	happen	next.
At	 midnight	 he	 woke	 up	 Bombur;	 and	 then	 in	 turn
rolled	 himself	 up	 in	 his	 corner,	 without	 listening	 to	 the
old	dwarf’s	thanks	(which	he	felt	he	had	hardly	earned).
He	was	soon	fast	asleep	forgetting	all	his	worries	till	the
morning.	As	a	matter	of	fact	he	was	dreaming	of	eggs	and
bacon.
